name: markdown-language-plumbing
body: Add an `md` language id and wire it into the scanner plumbing: (a) the auto-detection candidate list — add `("md", &[".md", ".markdown"])` to `auto_detect_languages`; (b) the `available_languages()` probe — `auto_detect_languages` selects a candidate only when it is present in the installed-frontend list (`available.iter().any(|l| l == lang)`, src/main.rs:499), so `available_languages()` (src/main.rs:370–401) must probe the md frontend artifact alongside the six existing frontend probes, using the probe form the md artifact actually needs (a bare-binary exists-check, or a directory/Node-script form matching `frontend_cmd`); an md candidate added alone can never fire; (c) the `lang_switch` control record that drives per-record code-type classification and FQN rendering; (d) the `--id-prefix` namespacing entry (`id_prefix_for`) so merged multi-language scans keep opaque ids unique; (e) the runtime frontend-command resolution (`frontend_cmd`) for the md frontend — a Node/Go-script artifact needs its own match branch (e.g. the `node <script>` form the ts arm uses). Directory exclusions during auto-detection are exactly the `has_extension` skip set — hidden dot entries, `target`, and `node_modules`; `vendor` and `gen` are NOT skipped by that helper, so the implementation must state/extend that exclusion set explicitly or reuse the scan-exclusion rule, rather than assume generated/dependency directories are already skipped. AC: a markdown-only repo auto-detects md; a mixed repo scans md alongside its code languages into one graph; the md stream carries its own id prefix and lang_switch record.
